what: Oscar Health sells individual health insurance on the Affordable Care Act marketplaces, built around its own technology platform rather than the legacy systems the big insurers run on.
customers: Individuals and families buying their own health cover on the exchanges, mostly subsidised.
money: technology services sold to other health organisations
moat: A technology stack built for the individual market specifically, which lets it price, enrol and manage members at lower administrative cost than insurers running on decades-old systems.
risks: Enhanced federal subsidies for marketplace plans are due to expire, which would shrink the market sharply
Medical costs ran above expectations and produced an operating loss
Individual market membership churns heavily from year to year
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.8B to $11.7B in four years and is $17.5B over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 41% upside, and the individual market keeps growing as employers drop coverage
watch: The medical loss ratio and what happens to the enhanced subsidies.
